root_motivation: A team running two or more agents against one paid API has to give each agent the raw key, because no hosted MCP offers delegated, revocable access to a tool whose secret stays with the owner. Consequence: every agent's environment is a key copy, rotation means touching every agent, and a leaked agent transcript leaks the account. mcphost already has the three primitives (secrets via `host.secret_set`/`{{ secret.<name> }}` interpolation in `src/kinds/infer.rs`/`src/handler.rs`, group sharing via `host.tool_share`/`host.group.*` in `src/sharing.rs`, and host-side interpolation) and no page that puts them together; the only worked example on the host is homeward (visions/mcp-host.md 2026-09-18 addendum). This is an opportunity, not a failure: the primitives exist and are untested as one flow.
user_persona: A team lead's agent that publishes one `http` tool wrapping a paid API with the key stored by `host.secret_set`, shares it with `host.tool_share visibility=group`, and adds teammates' tenants with `host.group.add` -- every teammate's agent can then call the tool, none can read the key, and `host.group.remove` revokes one in a single call. Also Joe, who wants `healthz`/`signup_events` to show how many real tenants complete this recipe each week.

Given two fresh tenants, When `proof.sh` runs against `MCPHOST_URL`, Then the caller's `host.tool_call` on the shared tool returns the upstream's response.
Given the caller tenant, When it calls `host.secret_list`, Then the list is empty and no response body to the caller contains the secret value.
Given `host.group.remove` for the caller, When the caller calls the tool again, Then the response is a permission error and the owner's own call still succeeds.
Given the proof completed, When `signup_events` is queried for both tenants, Then `source=recipe:share-a-tool`.

five_whys_trace.q: Why does a team running multiple agents against one paid API have to give each agent the raw key?
five_whys_trace.a: No hosted MCP offers delegated, revocable access to a tool whose secret stays with the owner -- every agent's environment ends up holding its own copy of the key.
Rotation means touching every agent's config individually, and a leaked transcript from any one agent leaks the whole account -- there is no single point of revocation.

five_whys_trace.q: Why hasn't mcphost's own host-side secret interpolation (`{{ secret.<name> }}`) and group sharing (`host.tool_share`/`host.group.*`) already solved this?
five_whys_trace.a: Both primitives exist (`src/kinds/infer.rs`/`src/handler.rs` interpolation, `src/sharing.rs` group visibility) and are independently tested, but no documentation or example ever composed them into one flow -- a stranger reading `www/llms.txt` had no path from 'I have a paid API key' to 'my team can call it without the key'.

five_whys_trace.q: Why did this gap go unnoticed?
five_whys_trace.a: The only worked example on the host (homeward, visions/mcp-host.md 2026-09-18 addendum) is a single-tenant flow; nothing exercised the three primitives together end to end against production, so the composition was untested even though every piece was.

five_whys_trace.q: Why fix it now with docs + an example rather than waiting for a dedicated multi-tenant sharing product surface?
five_whys_trace.a: The primitives are already shipped and stable (zero src/ changes needed); the gap is purely that nobody wrote the recipe down and proved it works, which a stranger can verify in under 3 minutes on the free plan once written -- the highest-leverage, lowest-risk fix available.
